A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cat metHb adopts an R-like tertiary structure and a T-like quaternary structure.

the T-state structure of cat metHb is stabilized by several unique features, including the formation of a novel salt bridge and the absence of a salt bridge that is commonly observed in other T-state Hbs.

the low oxygen-affinity of cat metHb is a result of a combination of the T-state-like quater-nary structure, the absence of the R-state-like tertiary-structural features in the distal haem environment, and the presence of the R-state tertiary-structural features at the interface between subunits.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the T-state structure is not a rigid structure but rather a flexible one that can accommodate several different tertiary and quaternary structural features, which may be important in understanding the mechanism of allostery.
the quaternary con-formation of Hb does not determine its ligand-binding properties.

the quaternary structure of the T state of cat metHb can be considered as a `quaternary template' for the low oxygen-affinity group of Hb, which may help to guide future studies of this group of proteins.
